predecessors.name: Umayyad Caliphate
predecessors.text: al-Andalus, the Iberian rump of the Umayyad realm after the Abbasid revolution; Yusuf was governor from 747

successors.name: Emirate of Córdoba
successors.text: Córdoba and the south, taken by Abd al-Rahman in 756; the centre and north follow in 779-783

ledger.x: 750: the Umayyads fall at Damascus and Yusuf al-Fihri keeps power in Spain.
September 755: Abd al-Rahman lands at Almuñécar and takes Málaga and then Seville 'without violence' by early 756.
March 756: Yusuf is defeated at the battle of Musarah 'just outside Córdoba in March 756'; Abd al-Rahman enters Córdoba and becomes 'the first independent Emir of Córdoba'.
14 May 756: Abd al-Rahman's reign begins with Córdoba and the south; Yusuf fled to Toledo.
779: 'until 779 (submission of Zaragoza)' Yusuf's supporters held large parts of the north; Abd al-Rahman gave Zaragoza's governorship to al-Husayn ibn Yahya and took it by force in 783.
779: the last of the Fihrid party submits; local leaders (Sulayman al-Arabi) had met Charlemagne's envoys in 777-778 against Abd al-Rahman, which the Upper March lords (777-783) dossier should carry.

wars.name: Abd al-Rahman I's conquest of al-Andalus
wars.outcome: Abd al-Rahman landed at Almuñécar in September 755, took Seville by March 756 and beat Yusuf at Musarah in March 756; the north and centre resisted until 779-783.

certainty.note: Al-Andalus before 756 is drawn from Cliopatria's shape; the supporters' territory after 756 is a reading of the pages' towns.
